# Cost and pricing

Model compute, database, cache, storage, backup, queue or stream, API gateway or load balancer, ingress and egress, cross-zone and cross-region transfer, observability, security services, support, and operational labor where material.

Use launch, target, and extreme scenarios. Show monthly total, cost per one million requests or active user when meaningful, dominant cost drivers, and sensitivity to traffic, payload, retention, replication, cache hit rate, and observability volume.

## Pricing evidence

Prefer official provider pricing APIs or documentation. Record provider, service, SKU, region, currency, unit, effective date, retrieval time, URL/API, purchase model, and exclusions. Retail estimates do not equal an invoice. Do not assume free tier, spot capacity, reservations, savings plans, enterprise discounts, taxes, or support discounts.

Use these statuses:

- `LIVE_ESTIMATE`: current official price with complete dimensions.
- `REVIEWED_SNAPSHOT`: reviewed local price still inside its validity window.
- `STALE`: price is older than its review window or service dimensions changed.
- `PARTIAL`: some material components or transfer paths lack prices.
- `UNAVAILABLE`: no defensible price source exists.

Pricing lookup failure never changes an unavailable estimate into zero. Compare architectural unit demand even when currency cost is unavailable.
